message: StaffMemberDrawer.tsx now renders the Employment Type row via transformAssignmentCategoryGroup(assignmentCategoryGroup, t) instead of the hardcoded pendingField placeholder, but StaffMemberDrawer.test.tsx has no assertion on this row for either a populated or null assignmentCategoryGroup. A regression that reverts this line to pendingField would not be caught by any test.

MpdAssignmentCategoryGroupEnum is mapped to display labels in two places: the new transformAssignmentCategoryGroup helper and the filter panel MenuItem children. The repo rule is one enum value maps to one label, so the dropdown and the row/drawer can drift apart on the next copy change.

transformAssignmentCategoryGroup already returns early for null/undefined, so the trailing default branch is unreachable for every value the type allows. It converts a future schema enum member from a compile error into a silent em dash in the UI.
dismissalDetail: the default branch is a deliberate runtime fallback for server enum values the client doesn't know yet; the unreachable-branch defect is gone (the early null return was removed) and helpers.test.ts covers the unknown-value path

message: The test is named "omits assignmentCategoryGroup" but it asserts the variable is sent as an explicit null, so it does not actually prove the argument is omitted.

Test is named 'omits assignmentCategoryGroup until an employment type is chosen' but the assertion checks that the variable is sent with value null, not that the key is omitted from the operation — the name and the behavior it verifies do not match.
The JSDoc comment on transformAssignmentCategoryGroup only restates the function name/signature and adds no non-obvious why, which this repo has repeatedly asked reviewers to trim.

The repo keeps localized enum-label helpers as getLocalizedX in src/lib/functions; this one is named transformAssignmentCategoryGroup and lives in a feature helpers file. Harmless today because the enum is used only here, but it makes the helper hard to find if a second feature needs the same label.

pendingField is documented as "Stands in for fields managedStaff cannot supply yet", but it is now also the placeholder for a field the API does supply as null. Grepping pendingField no longer tells you which fields are still unimplemented.

The Monthly Gross Salary warning marker is rendered with focusable=false inside a CardActionArea that already has an explicit aria-label, so keyboard and screen-reader users tabbing through the report get no indication a staff member has this warning — only sighted mouse users who hover the red icon see it.

healthStatusLabel re-maps MpdHealthStatusEnum to the same four labels as the existing healthLabel in helpers.ts, differing only in case. That breaks the repo rule of one label per enum value: the two copies of the text can drift apart and add a second set of translation keys.

The legend hardcodes the fiscal-quarter month ranges as translated strings, although this same PR adds getQuarterMonthRange to helpers.ts to compute them. There are now two definitions of the fiscal calendar that can disagree.

The chip delete control is given role="button" and an aria-label but no tabIndex or onKeyDown, so assistive tech announces it as an actionable button that cannot actually be activated from the keyboard.

suppressErrors is applied to the whole ManagedStaff operation, but the report only renders staffError when the list is empty, so a failed load-more page (fetchMore, not caught) is now completely silent. It also skips reportGraphQLError in client.ts, so every non-FILTER_REQUIRED server error on this query stops reaching Rollbar/Datadog.

pageSize 100 assumes one page holds the whole result, but the API clamps `first` to 50 (MPDXSchema default_max_page_size 50; ManagedStaffQuery sets no max_page_size). For 51-100 staff, TeamSummary counts and spouse merging run over only the first 50 people until the user scrolls to trigger loadMore, so the summary cards show wrong per-team status counts.

grossSalaryWarning() and QuickGlance both evaluate only the primary staff member of a merged spouse row (member.quarterlyHealth, member.newStaffMonthlySalary come from the spread `...node`, never `partner`), so a merged partner whose own Monthly Gross Salary is below their own New Staff benchmark never triggers the warning or shows their own gross-salary figure.

t("{{count}} {{status}}", { count }) was added to translation.json as a bare key with no _one/_other suffixes, unlike every other count-driven key in this file. i18next will not find a pluralized form for this key, so the per-status count chip (e.g. "1 at risk") risks rendering the literal key or the wrong plural form, and yarn extract will re-split it into suffixed keys on the next run, silently dropping the flat key added here.

getLocalizedSecaStatus is a second SecaStatusEnum localizer; getLocalizedTaxStatus already exists and labels the same values differently ("Subject to SECA"/"Subject to FICA"/"Exempt" vs "Pays SECA"/"Pays FICA"/"Exempt from SECA"). HR staff now see two wordings for one enum value across HrTools.

The pendingField fallback branches in QuickGlance (empty departments array, null geographicLocation, null newStaffMonthlySalary) are new to this component and are never exercised: the only quick-glance test (StaffMember.test.tsx "shows the extra details when expanded") uses a fully-populated member fixture.

The team summary is derived from staffMembers, which is already filtered server-side by teamNames/search/department, so clicking a card collapses the strip to that team (plus partial counts for any other teams its members share). The cards cannot be used to switch team to team, and the "overview" changes with every unrelated filter.

useManagedStaffTeamsQuery() destructures only `data`, not `error`; a failed teams query silently returns teamCount = 0 and the whole Teams section disappears with no indication anything went wrong, even for a supervisor who genuinely has several teams.

QuickGlance.tsx calls t('Department') for the department label, but translation.json only has the pre-existing "Department: {{department}}" key, not a bare "Department" key — this diff omits the new key the mined i18n rule requires to be hand-added alongside its first t() call.

The summarizeTeams sort test only exercises the red- and yellow-count tiebreakers (Gamma/Beta/Alpha), never the final alphabetical tiebreak (`a.name.localeCompare(b.name)`) for two teams with equal red/yellow counts.

QuickGlance.tsx is a new non-trivial component (142 lines, formats currency/quarter/enum data) but has no colocated QuickGlance.test.tsx; its behavior is only exercised indirectly through StaffMember.test.tsx, so edge cases specific to QuickGlance (e.g. department de-duplication across partner teams, missing partner spouse fallback) have no direct unit coverage.

Unmerged-spouse name formatting (spouseFirstName + spouseLastName ?? lastName) is written twice, in QuickGlance.tsx:58 and StaffMember.tsx:104, while the other row-name rules live in helpers.ts (getRowName). A future change to spouse naming will have to find both copies.

Monthly Gross Salary below benchmark is flagged by coloring the value text `error.main` in addition to the existing GrossSalaryMarker icon+tooltip. The row view (StaffMember.tsx) only ever used the icon marker, never a red value, so this is a new, inconsistent way of signalling the same warning.
dismissalDetail: Matches the drawer, which already colours the value red beside the marker; UX retracted in debate

message: QuickGlance always renders a "Spouse" detail line when `partner` is set (merged row), duplicating the combined name already shown in the row header per the design spec ("Merged rows already carry both names"), but no test covers the merged-pair QuickGlance output to confirm or refute this.
The new error Alert has no retry action, so the only way to recover is a full page reload. The mined PR-history rule asks for an Alert with a retry affordance in place of the report.

The whole mocks object is now cast with `as ApolloErgonoMockMap`, so the typed GqlMockedProvider generic no longer checks the happy-path mockData in any test in this file. A misspelled or stale field in mockData would now compile and be silently ignored.

In supervisor view, a failed report leaves staffName undefined and dataLoading false, so AccountInfoBox renders an empty name line above the error Alert. It reads like a render bug next to the new error state.

The error branch is tested only as a dead end; no test covers recovery when the user picks another year from the header, which stays enabled in the error state. A change that latches the error (for example storing it in state) would leave the alert up forever and still pass.
The Try Again button has no disabled/loading guard, so a user can click it repeatedly while a refetch is in flight, firing overlapping requests.
dismissalDetail: loading never turns true during a refetch after an error, and Apollo already merges repeated clicks into the one request in flight

message: ExportCsvButton and the Print button stay enabled during reportError, letting the user export an empty CSV or print a blank report instead of being blocked like the sibling MPGA error-state PR did.
dismissalDetail: Export CSV and Print are not rendered when the query fails, since there is no data and so no transactions; returning to a loaded month is served from cache without a new request, so an error never appears next to old data
